claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

apprenticeship_location.description: The country where the child has started an apprenticeship, where relevant.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions.

First, let me check the official guidance to ensure I provide you with accurate information.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for your patience. Now I can help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit.

Let me start with the first question:

**Do you have any children that you're responsible for?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do. I have a son, Alex. He's 19 and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I can see that Alex is 19 years old and lives with you.

Since Alex is over 16, I need to ask:

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?**

(This could include things like A-levels, certain college courses, or approved training programmes)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in college or anything like that. He actually started an apprenticeship recently, though.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to clarify something important about the apprenticeship:

**Did Alex start an apprenticeship in England, or is it in Scotland, Wales, or Northern Ireland?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's in Scotland - he's doing it in Dundee.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information.

Based on what you've told me, I now have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me summarize the situation:
- You have a son named Alex who is 19 years old
- Alex lives at home with you
- Alex is not in approved education or training
- Alex has started an apprenticeship in Scotland (Dundee)

According to the official guidance I've reviewed, Child Benefit stops when a child starts an apprenticeship **in England**. However, Alex's apprenticeship is in Scotland, not England.

Before I provide my final assessment, let me ask one more question to ensure I have complete information:

**Is Alex working 24 hours or more per week, or is he receiving any benefits in his own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working that many hours - the apprenticeship keeps him busy but it's not a full-time job like that. And no, he doesn't get any benefits himself.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for providing all that information. I now have sufficient details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

While Child Benefit normally stops when a young person aged 16-19 starts an apprenticeship, the rules specifically state this applies to apprenticeships **in England**. Since Alex's apprenticeship is in Scotland (Dundee), this disqualification doesn't apply to your situation.

Alex is:
- Under 20 years old (he's 19)
- Living at home with you
- Not working 24+ hours per week
- Not receiving benefits in his own right

All of these factors mean you continue to qualify for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Please note:** If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge, though you would still be eligible to claim the benefit itself.

If you have any other questions about Child Benefit, please feel free to ask!
